plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: lighter manual jobs (courier, messenger, car park attendant, watchman) that can be managed by the right hand

injuries.description: 20 cm laceration over medial side of left upper arm

there was left wrist laceration and cut of superficing branch of radial nerve.

source: Doctors later found complete cut of median nerve, brachial artery and vein, musculocutaneous nerve, biceps, branchialis and common nerve origin. Vascular repair and muscle repair was performed.
On 10 November 2008, plaintiff was found to have acute tear of brachial artery and median nerve and bicep-tendon.

source: there was left wrist laceration and cut of superficing branch of radial nerve.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of radial nerve at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: sacrifice of the sural nerve for median nerve grafting (resulting in left leg numbness over dorsum of outer 3 toes)
source: Plaintiff complained also of left numbness, over dorsum of outer 3 toes. It was said that the same was due to sacrifice of the sural nerve for median nerve grafting.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of cutaneous sensory nerve at ankle or foot level

manifestations.description: left upper arm and fingers still in pain and rigid
numbness in left arm and fingers; diffuse sensation loss over forearm and hand, sparing the ulnar side; decreased sensation over left thumb and index finger
cannot bend or flex left arm; decreased range of motion over shoulder, elbow, wrist and fingers
left arm feels weak and no strength; grasping ability of left hand greatly decreased; power generally weaker, in particular with flexion
injuries affecting his sleep at night; unable to sleep at night; stress and depressed
extensive scarring; long surgical scar from the medial side of anterior arm to wrist which was tender on touch; scar appeared red and raised
persistent numbness at anterior left forearm and 1st to 3rd fingers with nil pain sensation
left leg numbness over dorsum of outer 3 toes
loss of dexterity; loss of ability to handle activities of daily life independently with difficulty performing tasks such as holding a rice bowl, buttoning a shirt, wrenching a towel
reduced muscle bulk: thinner left arm and forearm muscles
acute distress disorder (subclinical level) / persistent fear and flashback

treatments_received: tendon transfer (Palmaris longus to distal bicep)
physiotherapy (multiple modalities: microcurrent therapy, whirlpool exercise, ultrasound therapy, electrical stimulation, exercise therapy, reconditioning exercise)
occupational therapy (splintage treatment, pressure treatment, remedial activities, work hardening program)

losses.description: Residual weakness, loss of strength and dexterity of the left upper limb and hand resulting from tendon ruptures and nerve cuts (affecting ability to grasp, lift and flex the left arm)
Long surgical scar from medial side of anterior arm to wrist, tender on touch and cosmetically conspicuous causing discomfort when wearing short sleeves

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Inability to hold heavy objects, cannot hold a rice bowl, difficulty buttoning a shirt or wrenching a towel
Unable to return to pre-accident demolition/renovation work requiring strength and use of both hands; limited to lighter manual jobs manageable by the right hand
acute distress disorder (subclinical level) / persistent fear and flashback
